facts.claim: On Arch, partial upgrades are unsupported: 'pacman -Sy <pkg>' (refresh index without upgrading everything) can break the system. JARVIS therefore never runs bare '-Sy'; its refresh playbook warns and its upgrade uses '-Syu'.

sources.ref: Arch Wiki: System maintenance — partial upgrades

facts.claim: Non-interactive apt runs must set DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive (and ideally DEBIAN_PRIORITY=critical) or debconf may block on interactive prompts; JARVIS sets both env vars for every apt mutation.
apt(8) is the friendly interactive front-end whose output/behavior may change between releases; apt-get(8) is the stable interface intended for scripts — which is why JARVIS drives apt-get, not apt.

'systemctl is-active <unit>' exits 0 when the unit is active and 3 (not 1) when none are active — scripts must treat any non-zero as not-active. JARVIS's service playbooks use exactly these semantics.
